text:
rachel: heads-up — bringing up thalassa-14b (int4) canary. hitting warm-start OOMs on long single-stream gens (>=1200 tokens). fragmentation metric (gpu_heap_frag) skyrockets after first large request and doesn't drop.
deploy-bot: Canary deployed: thalassa-14b-int4 @ pool-delta (10 replicas).
anya: repro: single-client chat, target length ~1300-1500 tokens, seen on both A100 and H100 instances. microbatch=1 reproduces fastest.
leo: can you paste the tiny log snippet where it OOMs?
rachel: sure — here's the allocator slice at fail:
```
[E] cudaMalloc failed: OutOfMemory
alloc requested 1.12GiB for attn_kv
post-oom: free_chunks=11, largest_free=56MiB
heap_trend: 2.0GiB -> 1.6GiB -> 360MiB
```
ciara: that pattern matches KV-slot churn + free-list fragmentation we've seen on other 14b int4 brings. quick wins: lower default max_new_tokens, disable prefetch on warm path, enable slab compaction on eviction.
ben: agree. also suggest a "startup primer" request (e.g. 80-100 tokens) to allocate KV shapes early, and a conservative microbatching window (20ms) to consolidate short bursts without raising p95 too much.
leo: propose concrete defaults for the model config:
- max_new_tokens: 512
- prefetch: false on warm-start
- kv_eviction_threshold: 0.6
- slab_compact_on_eviction: true
- startup_prime: true (80 tokens)
ciara: add metric collection: alloc_histogram + free_chunk_count every 5m, and capture any OOM trace (stack + alloc site). Also run conv-bench 1k prompts for quality (Rouge/LLMScore).
rachel: I'll kick off an A/B canary: control = baseline config; variant = leo's config. 8h run, long-gen workload. Command:
```
./canary_tool --model thalassa-14b --quant int4 \
  --ctrl "max_new=1024,prefetch=true,slab_compact=false" \
  --var  "max_new=512,prefetch=false,kv_thresh=0.6,slab_compact=true,startup_prime=80" \
  --duration 8h --collect alloc_hist:5m --collect frag_metrics:5m
```
ben: I'll watch for OOM rate, fragmentation timeline, and quality deltas. rollout plan if variant stable: canary -> 30% (24h) -> 60% (24h) -> 100% with FP16 fallback if OOM rate > 0.5% or P95 latency regresses >20%.
anya: if we still see tail OOMs after this, next steps: kernel affinity for allocator thread, small page-alignment allocator patch, or increasing per-slot eviction aggressiveness.
leo: ping infra to reserve 2 debug nodes in case we need live cudaMalloc traces. @rachel include the plots when done.
rachel: starting run now, will post results + plots at 6123464000. :thumbsup:
